title-group.article-title: Analytical validation of a methylation-specific PCR assay for SEPT9 in colorectal cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Riverside University Medical Center, Chicago, IL
Central Oncology Research Hospital, Houston, TX
Westlake Comprehensive Cancer Center, Seattle, WA

abstract.p: Background: Detection of SEPT9 promoter methylation is clinically relevant in colorectal cancer, but routine testing can be limited by turnaround time, tissue availability, and workflow complexity. We developed and analytically validated a methylation-specific PCR assay for rapid molecular testing. Methods: The assay was designed to detect three methylated SEPT9 regions using plasma-derived cell-free DNA. Analytical sensitivity, specificity, precision, reproducibility, reportable range, and limit of detection were evaluated with reference materials, contrived specimens, and residual clinical samples. Testing used a minimum input of 12 ng. Orthogonal concordance was assessed against bisulfite sequencing. Results: The assay achieved a limit of detection of 0.35% methylated allele fraction. Overall analytical sensitivity was 95.8% and analytical specificity was 98.7%. Across 11 independent runs, the median coefficient of variation was 8.1%. Results were reproducible across operators, reagent lots, and instruments. Agreement with bisulfite sequencing was 95.2%, with discordant samples concentrated near the analytical detection limit. Conclusions: This methylation-specific PCR assay provides sensitive, specific, and reproducible detection of SEPT9 promoter methylation in colorectal cancer. The workflow may offer a practical alternative or complement to existing molecular methods when rapid results or limited specimen input are important. Prospective clinical validation is ongoing. Research Sponsor: Institutional innovation award.
